correctness.rationale: An analytic cubic edge-count inequality gives the lower bound four and forces each optimal four-set to be independent with tree complement. The direct_check.js verifier enumerates every four-subset of fourteen vertices and tests complement acyclicity by disjoint-set union; cycle_check.js independently generates all simple cycles and tests cycle hitting. They agree on all 70 states and independently enumerate the move graphs and all-sources BFS metrics; their embedded outputs reproduce the claimed 14 isolated, 14 K2 and 7 P4 slide components, connected four-regular jump graph of diameter seven and radius six, and the n=5,6 cutoff. Exact finite enumeration is a proof of the finite claim, not an infinite generalization.

These antecedents do not by their inspected statements give the GP(7,2) token-slide component classification, jump graph metric, or initial mixed-mobility cutoff. No equivalent result was located in searched scientific records, with unindexed or unavailable complete prior literature retained as a priority risk.

value.rationale: A motivated complete finite classification of optimum cycle-breaking placements in the first three generalized Petersen graphs of step two, identifying the first coexistence of frozen and movable minima under local slides. It sharply separates local accessibility (35 components) from unrestricted reachability (one component and known exact diameter), a natural sensor/vertex-deletion reconfiguration invariant not determined by the scalar decycling number. The result is valuable as a structural boundary without a claimed infinite extension.
